issues.body: `sparq_gpu_is_still_unpublished` still checks only whether a comment-stripped line starts with `publish` and contains `false`. A valid unrelated key such as `publish-note = false` satisfies that predicate even if `publish = false` is removed or changed to `publish = true`. Cargo would then treat the package as publishable while this deferral trigger remains green, contradicting the enforcement claims in `lib.rs` and `research/threat-model.md`.
issues.fix_hint: Reuse Cargo metadata: select the `sparq-gpu` workspace package by package identity and require its `publish` field to be an empty array, Cargo metadata's representation of `publish = false`. Add a focused regression fixture proving that an absent or true `publish` setting plus an unrelated `publish-note = false` key is rejected.
issues.title: Publication tripwire still accepts unrelated manifest keys

verdict.summary: Round 4's major finding remains unchanged. The dependency detector now uses Cargo metadata, but `sparq_gpu_is_still_unpublished` still scans manifest text with `starts_with("publish") && contains("false")`. An unrelated key such as `publish-note = false` can therefore keep the tripwire green after `publish = false` is removed or changed, despite the documentation claiming publication is enforced. Progress is stagnant because the same major correctness/security-enforcement gap remains at the same severity.
